meta.primarySource: J.P. Morgan Asset Management, 2026 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, 30th Annual Edition. USD assumption matrix.
meta.returnBasis: nominal, compound (geometric), net of fees where the source states it
meta.note: Not one number below was produced by this project. Every return, volatility and correlation is read from the J.P. Morgan matrix cited above. J.P. Morgan revises these every year and has revised them by more than a percentage point in a single year. They are a considered view, not a fact.

crossChecks.name: Vanguard Capital Markets Model, 10-year annualised, simulation date 30 June 2026
crossChecks.examples: US equities 4.2 to 6.2 percent, global ex-US equities 3.9 to 5.9 percent, emerging markets 2.0 to 4.0 percent, US aggregate bonds 4.3 to 5.3 percent.

crossChecks.name: BlackRock Investment Institute capital market assumptions, data as of 30 June 2026
crossChecks.examples: US large cap 8.97 percent, emerging large cap 8.80 percent, global aggregate bonds hedged 4.51 percent.

crossChecks.name: UBS Global Investment Returns Yearbook 2026 (Dimson, Marsh, Staunton), 1900 to 2025
crossChecks.examples: US equities 6.6 percent real per year and 9.8 percent nominal over 126 years. US bonds 1.6 percent real. US bills 0.5 percent real. Gold 1.3 percent real since 1900.

meta.disagreement: On emerging markets equity, J.P. Morgan says 7.8 percent, BlackRock says 8.8 percent, and Vanguard says 2.0 to 4.0 percent. That spread is roughly five percentage points a year on the same asset class over the same horizon. Anyone who tells you the expected return of an asset class to one decimal place is telling you about their model, not about the future.

assetClasses.label: Cash and Treasury bills
assetClasses.plain: Money you can spend tomorrow. Earns a little, loses to inflation slowly.

assetClasses.label: Short government bonds
assetClasses.plain: Lending to the US government for a few years. Safer than shares, pays more than cash.

assetClasses.label: Global bonds, currency hedged
assetClasses.plain: Lending to governments around the world, with the currency risk stripped out.

assetClasses.label: Inflation-linked bonds
assetClasses.plain: Government bonds whose payments rise with US inflation. Protects purchasing power, not price.

assetClasses.label: Global shares
assetClasses.plain: Part ownership of thousands of companies worldwide. The main engine of long-run growth.

assetClasses.label: Emerging market shares
assetClasses.plain: Companies in faster-growing, less stable economies. Higher expected return, bigger swings.

assetClasses.label: Listed property
assetClasses.plain: Shares in companies that own and rent out buildings. Behaves mostly like shares, not like a house.

assetClasses.label: Gold
assetClasses.plain: Owned by no government and issued by no bank. Pays you nothing and can go nowhere for a decade.
